item.title: Woman wanted after Picayune meth bust; man charged with trafficking - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PICAYUNE – A Picayune man was arrested Monday after authorities executed a search warrant at a residence on West Lakeshore Drive and found methamphetamine, drug packaging materials and cash, according to the Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department.

The sheriff’s department said deputies with the Narcotics Division, assisted by the SWAT Team, Criminal Investigations Division and Patrol Division, served the warrant around 5:55 a.m. April 6 at the home of Jack Ceaser, 46, and Jessica Stewart, 42, at 726 W. Lakeshore Drive.

Investigators said the warrant was the result of a lengthy investigation prompted by numerous community complaints about suspected drug trafficking at the residence.

According to authorities, Ceaser was inside the home when deputies arrived and was seen attempting to destroy evidence. He was taken into custody without incident.

A search of the residence turned up what officials described as an aggravating quantity of methamphetamine, along with plastic baggies, a digital scale and a large amount of cash.

Ceaser was taken to the Pearl River County Correctional Facility and charged with felony aggravated trafficking of a controlled substance and tampering with physical evidence.

Authorities said Stewart was not at the residence when the warrant was served. A warrant will be issued charging her with felony aggravated trafficking of a controlled substance.

Sheriff David Allison praised the work of the Narcotics Division, SWAT Team, Criminal Investigations Division and Patrol Division, and thanked community members for reporting suspected drug trafficking activity.

Anyone with narcotics tips is asked to call 601-403-2582.

item.title: Woman sentenced to 30 years after pleading guilty to attempted murder in Prentiss County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
IUKA – A woman was sentenced Wednesday to 30 years in prison after pleading guilty to attempted murder and aggravated assault in separate Prentiss County cases, according to the First Circuit Court District attorney’s office.

District Attorney Jason D. Herring said Veronica Gillespie pleaded guilty April 8, 2026, to attempted murder in connection with an Aug. 26, 2023, incident in Prentiss County. Gillespie also pleaded guilty to one count of aggravated assault stemming from a Nov. 8, 2022, incident in the county.

After accepting the guilty pleas, Circuit Court Judge Kelly Mims sentenced Gillespie to 40 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections on the attempted murder charge, with 10 years suspended, leaving 30 years to serve.

On the aggravated assault charge, Gillespie was sentenced to 20 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections, with all 20 years suspended. Prosecutors said that sentence will run consecutive to the sentence imposed in the attempted murder case.

The district attorney’s office recognized Booneville Police Department Detective Karl Courtney for his work on the investigations.

The cases were prosecuted by Assistant District Attorneys Joel Baldwin and Reagan Wise on behalf of the state.

item.title: Wanted man arrested after brief Capitol Police pursuit in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – A man wanted by the U.S. Marshals Service was arrested Tuesday after leading Capitol Police on a brief pursuit in Jackson, according to authorities.

Officials said officers attempted to stop a vehicle around 2:21 p.m. because it had no tag. The driver did not stop and led officers on a short chase that ended near Woodrow Wilson Avenue and Martin Luther King Jr. Drive.

Authorities identified the driver as 36-year-old Jarvaris Davis. After the vehicle stopped, Davis tried to run but was quickly apprehended without further incident.

According to authorities, Davis was wanted through the U.S. Marshals Service. Investigators also found the vehicle he was driving had been reported stolen.

Davis is charged with felony fleeing and possession of a stolen vehicle.

item.title: Suspect wanted in Hinds County carjacking arrested after Yazoo pursuit - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
YAZOO COUNTY – A man wanted on carjacking charges out of Hinds County is in custody after a pursuit that began near Yazoo City, according to the Yazoo County Sheriff’s Office.

The suspect was identified as Kalveonte Moore.

The sheriff’s office said Investigator Antwan Jones saw the suspect’s vehicle traveling north on Highway 49 as it entered the Yazoo City limits. Deputies then made contact with the vehicle, but the driver refused to stop, leading officers to begin a pursuit.

According to the sheriff’s office, Moore was wanted in Hinds County on carjacking charges. Authorities also said the vehicle he was driving was confirmed stolen and has since been recovered.

The pursuit ended without injuries, the sheriff’s office said. Officials credited the coordinated efforts of multiple law enforcement agencies for bringing the incident to a safe conclusion.

Moore is being held at the Yazoo County Regional Correctional Facility.

item.title: Mississippi Blood Services announces urgent need for platelet donors - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Mississippi Blood Services is urging people to donate platelets as hospitals continue to rely on donations to treat patients in need.

The organization said platelet donations provide critical support for cancer patients, trauma cases and others requiring specialized care.

As an incentive, Mississippi Blood Services said donors who give platelets will receive a $50 Visa gift card.

Platelet donations can be made at Mississippi Blood Services locations in Flowood, Cleveland and Oxford. The Flowood donor center is located at 115 Tree St. The Cleveland center is at 609 N. Davis Ave., Suite 101B, and the Oxford center is at 2627 W. Oxford Loop, Suite C.

item.title: Arrests made, weapons seized in Jackson crackdown on Rebelwood violence - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Multiple arrests have been made and several weapons seized following a targeted law enforcement operation at the Rebelwood apartments, city officials announced Tuesday, part of an ongoing effort to curb violent crime in Jackson.

Jackson Police, working with federal partners including the U.S. Marshals Service, served three arrest warrants and executed two search warrants during the April 7 operation, Police Chief Dr. RaShall Brackney said. Authorities took four people into custody and recovered four firearms, including three AR-style pistols.

Those arrested include Isaac Gibson, 26; Frederick Williams, 23; Cordarius Beasley, 23; and Annie Smith, 49. Charges range from possession of a firearm by a convicted felon to murder, with bond set between $40,000 and no bond, Brackney said.

The enforcement action follows a pattern of violent crime at the complex, including two recent homicides. Brackney identified one victim as Travarius Cooper and said the area had generated hundreds of calls for service.

“This operation has removed dangerous individuals and illegal weapons from our streets, and we are not done yet,” Brackney said. “If you bring violence into Jackson, we will find you, we will arrest you, and we will hold you accountable.”

Officials said the investigation remains ongoing, with additional warrants outstanding and more arrests possible.

Authorities described those arrested in connection with the homicide as acquaintances, but declined to provide further details about possible gang affiliations, citing the active investigation.

During the operation, officers recovered multiple firearms, which Brackney said reduces opportunities for future violence. “That means there are four less opportunities to commit homicides and violence in our community,” she said.

Mayor John Horhn said the crackdown is part of a broader strategy targeting high-crime areas across the city.

“We’re going to tackle them one by one to make sure that we send a strong message that criminal activity, particularly violent activity, is not going to be condoned in the city of Jackson,” Horhn said.

Police said they will maintain a strong presence in the Rebelwood area and continue working with federal agencies, including the DEA and ATF, to address ongoing criminal activity. Officials also urged residents to come forward with information as the investigation continues.

item.title: MSU implements tool to help students with decision making, career planning - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
STARKVILLE — Mississippi State is pointing future and current students to a new university resource to help explore academic programs and select a major.

MSU is introducing Major Maps, a year-by-year roadmap containing information about each undergraduate major at the university. The online tool can help prospective students and their families understand what a major offers and what to expect from each academic pathway toward a bachelor’s degree. The information guide also is useful for career planning as it shows how each major positions graduates for future opportunities.

“Students and families alike are asking thoughtful questions about the value of a degree and how it connects to future opportunities. Major Maps helps answer these questions by presenting clear, consistent information about what students will study, how they can enrich that experience, and where that path can lead after graduation,” said MSU Provost and Executive Vice President David Shaw.

“Major Maps is a practical tool that supports students from the moment they begin exploring Mississippi State through graduation and beyond. By helping students better understand their academic options, stay on track in their programs, and connect their degree to future careers, this resource advances key priorities for how we support students at MSU,” he added.

Available at www.majors.msstate.edu , Major Maps supports several MSU goals, including serving as a strong support system to recruit prospective students to the state’s leading university, improve student retention and further increase employability by helping students better articulate the value of each degree. It also supports academic advising, giving students and advisors a shared, easy-to-read reference outlining important curricular milestones, suggested co-curricular experiences and ways students can stay on track academically.

Shelby Tschume, executive director for strategic initiatives in MSU’s Office of the Provost, said not only future and current students, but a broad variety of users will benefit from the streamlined information presented through Major Maps. From parents and family members to advisors, faculty and external partners, the tool offers clarity and consistency.

“This will be extremely helpful to anyone seeking accurate information about MSU majors, and we have designed this tool to feel welcoming, informative and easy to navigate. We want all our students to feel confident about the majors they are choosing and how they can make the most of their time at the university,” Tschume said. She also expressed appreciation for the collaborative effort among faculty, staff and college leaders in bringing the project to fruition.

Major Exploration Workshops co-hosted by the Career Center and the Center for Advising will assist students who are undecided on a major to compare different programs and learn how various options align with their personal interests, skills and career goals.

Mississippi State University is taking care of what matters. Learn more at www.msstate.edu.

item.title: ‘Squeeze the Day’ Fundraiser Returns to Support The Mustard Seed - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
BRANDON – The Mustard Seed has launched its annual “Squeeze the Day” fundraiser, encouraging supporters to host lemonade stands and donate proceeds to help adults with developmental disabilities and their families.

This year’s fundraiser runs from April 4 through May 30, according to promotional materials shared by the organization.

Organizers said the fundraiser is one of the many ways the community can support The Mustard Seed each year. Proceeds help the nonprofit continue its mission of serving more than 40 adults with developmental disabilities and their families.

In addition to raising financial support, organizers said the event also helps build awareness about The Mustard Seed and the people it serves, known as Seedsters.

Participants are encouraged to register their lemonade stands through The Mustard Seed and host a stand during the campaign period. Proceeds can then be donated to the organization at its location at 1085 Luckney Road in Brandon.

The campaign is supported by community partners including Watkins Construction & Roofing, Guaranty Bank and On Target.

item.title: Retired Jackson Public Schools educator Mary Robinson remembered for years of service - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Jackson Public Schools is mourning the loss of retired educator Mary Robinson, who spent many years serving students across the district.

According to Jackson Public Schools, Robinson worked at Smith Elementary, in Property Accounting and as a teacher in the Exceptional Education Department at Hardy Middle School and Capital City Alternative School.

The district said Robinson valued the relationships she built during her career and took pride in supporting both students and colleagues.

Her homegoing celebration was held April 4.

Jackson Public Schools said Robinson made a lasting impact on generations of students and expressed gratitude for her years of commitment to the district.

Her family has asked for continued thoughts and prayers during this time. Condolences may be shared through her online obituary.

item.title: Rankin County Sheriff's office looking for missing man after his wallet was found - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – The Rankin County Sheriff’s Department is looking for a missing 50-year-old man.

Charles “Derek” Mcleod Jr. was reported missing by his parents after someone found his wallet in Ridgeland and returned it to them.

Derek does not have a known vehicle, according to the sheriff’s department.

He has not been replying to phone calls or texts.

His family last saw him during Thanksgiving in 2025 at 107 Bailey Avenue Pearl, MS but he was working for a carpentry business in Ridgeland, MS as recently as January 2026.

Anyone with information on the whereabouts of Derek Mcleod should contacted the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department at 601-825-1480 or their local law enforcement agency.

item.title: Monticello Elementary briefly locked down after reported gunshot - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONTICELLO — Monticello Elementary School was placed on lockdown Tuesday morning after reports of a gunshot near campus, but Monticello Chief Sterling Allen said no threat was found.

The incident was reported around 8:48 a.m. April 7, prompting a response from the Monticello Police Department and the Lawrence County School District Police Department.

With assistance from the Lawrence County Sheriff’s Office, officers searched the area but did not locate any active threat.

The school was placed on lockdown as a precaution and has since been cleared, with normal operations resuming, Allen said.

He said additional security measures and resources will be in place throughout the day as a precaution.

“The safety of our children remains our highest priority,” Allen said.

This comes one day after an argument between groups led to a shootout in the parking lot of the Sonic in Monticello.

item.title: Four injured, two arrested after shooting at Monticello Sonic - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONTICELLO — Four people were injured and two suspects are in custody following a shootout Monday morning at a Sonic Drive-In in Monticello , authorities said.

Monticello Police Chief Sterling Allen said the incident began around 10:58 a.m. April 6, when he received a call about an active shooter at the Sonic on F.E. Sellers Drive.

“As I exited the police department, I heard what no law enforcement officer ever wants to hear… gunfire,” Allen said in a statement.

Officers with the Monticello Police Department and deputies from the Lawrence County Sheriff’s Office arrived within minutes, securing the scene and rendering aid to victims. Four individuals were struck by gunfire and injured. Their conditions have not been released.

According to Monticello Mayor Justin Mullins, the shooting stemmed from an argument between groups of people that escalated into gunfire. No bystanders were reported injured.

Authorities said multiple nearby businesses were also hit by gunfire during the incident.

Two arrests have been made, and additional arrests are expected as the investigation continues, Allen said in a release posted to Facebook around 3 a.m.

Emergency responders from multiple agencies assisted at the scene, including the Monticello Fire Department, Lawrence County Volunteer Fire Department, Life Guard Ambulance Service and Med Air. A helicopter was seen landing nearby, according to witnesses.

State and federal agencies, including the Mississippi Highway Patrol and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, are also involved in the investigation.

“This remains an active and ongoing investigation,” Allen said. “I urge anyone who witnessed this incident or has information to contact the Monticello Police Department.”

Anyone with information is asked to call the department at 601-587-7732.

item.title: Dog Rescued After Jackson Walgreens Break-In; Rescue Looking for Foster and Donations - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON — A dog is now receiving veterinary care after being found during the arrest of a man accused of breaking into a Walgreens in Jackson, according to local rescue Cheshire Abbey.

The group said Capitol Police discovered the dog trapped inside the building when officers went to arrest the suspect. Rescue volunteers were then contacted to take custody of the animal.

According to the rescue, the dog had not been properly cared for and is now being treated by a veterinarian. The group said it plans to restore the dog’s skin condition and provide full veterinary care, including spaying.

The rescue is now asking for a foster home for the dog, saying it currently has no available space. The group also said the person who fosters the dog will be able to name her.

In addition, the organization is requesting help covering veterinary and boarding expenses. Donations can be made through Venmo, PayPal or directly through its account at Florence Animal Clinic.

The rescue group also thanked Capitol Police for helping remove the dog from what it described as a situation of suffering.

item.title: Columbus Man Charged After Stabbing on Railroad Street - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COLUMBUS – A Columbus man has been charged after police say he stabbed another man during a physical altercation earlier this month.

According to the Columbus Police Department, officers responded April 3 to the 800 block of Railroad Street in reference to a stabbing.

When officers arrived, they rendered aid to 47-year-old William Jones, who had sustained multiple stab wounds to his upper body. Jones was transported for medical treatment.

During the investigation, officers determined that 45-year-old Tyshun Hudson stabbed Jones during a physical altercation, police said.

On April 4, an officer located Hudson and took him into custody without incident. He was transported to the Lowndes County Adult Detention Center.

Hudson has been charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.

The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with additional information is encouraged to contact the Columbus Police Department or Golden Triangle Crime Stoppers.

item.title: Warrior Bonfire Program to host fishing tournament April 18 - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
PEARL — Anglers and community members are invited to gather April 18 at the Ross Barnett Reservoir for a day of fishing and fundraising aimed at supporting Purple Heart recipients.

The Warrior Bonfire Crappie Tournament is scheduled to begin with lines in at 6:30 a.m., with participants launching from most public ramps around the reservoir. Registration closes at 7:30 a.m., and fishing will continue until 2 p.m., followed by a 3:30 p.m. weigh-in at Bass Pro Shops.

Organizers say proceeds from the tournament will benefit the Warrior Bonfire Program, a nonprofit that provides outdoor retreats and long-term support for post-9/11 Purple Heart recipients.

The event will feature a five-fish limit per boat, with prizes awarded to the top three finishers. First place will receive a $300 gift card and trophy, followed by $200 and $100 gift cards for second and third place, respectively. An optional “Big Fish Pot” will also be available, with a payout for the largest catch.

Beyond the competition, the event is designed as a community gathering to honor veterans and raise awareness of the program’s mission. The Warrior Bonfire Program focuses on activity-based, stress-free experiences that promote camaraderie and healing for service members wounded in combat.

Those who do not fish can still participate through a raffle open nationwide. Tickets are $20 each or six for $100, with prizes including Bass Pro Shops gift cards ranging from $100 to $500 and nearly two dozen additional giveaways. Winners will be announced during the weigh-in, and participants do not need to be present to win.

See the Warrior Bonfire Program on Amazon Prime

Event organizers said attendees can expect live updates throughout the day, an emcee, and appearances from local sponsors and the Mississippi Army National Guard. Food will also be available at the weigh-in, with Penn’s Fish House food truck serving fish and chicken.

Fishing is not permitted to launch from Madison Landing or Goshen Springs, but all other public ramps at the reservoir are open for the tournament.

Organizers said the event aims to combine outdoor recreation with a meaningful cause, emphasizing that “no warrior heals alone.”

item.title: Spring Cleaning Your Kitchen? Here's How to Keep Bugs Out - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
(StatePoint) With warmer weather here, spring cleaning and hosting season are in full swing. While you prep your home for guests, you may also be seeing an uptick of insect activity.

Unfortunately, insects tend to gather in the same areas of the home where household members and guests do – anywhere there is food. So, rather than let bugs disrupt your spring gatherings, act right away. Doing so is important, as insects reproduce rapidly. In fact, it only takes one week for two fruit flies to multiply to 500 fruit flies!

By using these tips to banish bugs from your kitchen this spring, you can enjoy the feeling you get when your space is truly clean and guest-ready:

Do a deep clean: In addition to regular kitchen upkeep, be sure to do a deep clean in spring and every time you host. This is a great way to finally tackle those corners, crevices and seldom-addressed surfaces in the fridge, oven and pantry, where pest-attracting food residue and grease can build up.

Catch what you can’t clean: A fly trap for indoors is a necessary addition to your kitchen spring cleaning and hosting routine. Zevo catches what you can’t clean – working continuously to trap those pesky flies and gnats that linger around sinks, trash cans, and countertops even after you’ve scrubbed. Simply plug in a Zevo Flying Insect Trap near high-traffic areas, such as near party spreads, fruit bowls or garbage, and doors that are opened throughout the day. Its blue and UV light attract and catch fruit flies, gnats, house flies and other flying insects 24/7 and its sleek, discreet design will look good in your kitchen.

“Plugging in a Zevo Insect Trap is an easy way to achieve that level of cleanliness you’re looking for, so you have more time for what matters – enjoying the spring season with friends and family,” says Rob Reinerman, Vice President of Procter & Gamble Ventures, parent company of Zevo, a line of worry-free pest solutions.

Fix leaks: If you have a leak under your kitchen sink, you may unwittingly be creating an inviting habitat for bugs, which are drawn to water sources. Fix the leak so you invite only human guests to your kitchen and home this spring. Doing so will have the added benefit of preventing water damage and mold.

Seal food tightly: Take a quick look at your pantry to assess your food storage containers. Transfer all items like flour and sugar out of paper packaging and into tightly-sealed jars. Not only will this help keep bugs at bay, but your essential ingredients will stay fresher for improved hosting.

For more information about pest control in the kitchen and other areas of your home, visit zevoinsect.com.

Maintaining a tidy kitchen is just the first step in banishing bugs. Simple additional measures that require very little effort can help you truly keep the spaces where you prep, host, and enjoy your food clean, fresh and insect-free.

Authorities said the stop happened around 7:15 p.m. Tuesday, March 17, on Jackson Landing Road near Lilac Drive. Deputies with the Patrol Division stopped a Chrysler 200 for an expired tag.

Sheriff David Allison said he wants the public to know deputies are continuing efforts to keep drugs off the streets.

item.title: New Beer’s Eve taps into history, celebration across Mississippi and beyond - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MISSISSIPPI — Before the first pour of National Beer Day on April 7, we raise a glass the night before, celebrating New Beer’s Eve, a holiday rooted in one of the most dramatic turnarounds in U.S. history.

Observed each year on April 6, New Beer’s Eve marks the moment in 1933 when legal beer returned after more than a decade of Prohibition. According to NationalToday.com, President Franklin D. Roosevelt ushered in the change, allowing Americans to once again drink, buy and sell alcohol legally.

The result was immediate and enthusiastic. NationalToday.com reports that Americans consumed about 1.5 million gallons of beer in the first 24 hours after Prohibition effectively ended, with crowds lining up outside bars and taverns for their first legal drink in nearly 13 years.

The celebration was about more than just beer, it was about connection and communication in a changing country. According to DaysOfTheYear.com, people gathered in pubs, restaurants and homes, eager to reconnect over a simple pleasure that had been banned since 1920 under the 18th Amendment.

Prohibition, which lasted from 1920 to 1933, outlawed the production and sale of alcohol nationwide. Britannica.com notes the ban created widespread demand for faster policy change as the nation faced economic hardship during the Great Depression and sought new sources of jobs and tax revenue.

When restrictions were lifted, even partially at first with low-alcohol beer, it jumpstarted breweries and related industries. Historical accounts cited by DaysOfTheYear.com indicate the return of beer helped revive manufacturing, agriculture and transportation sectors tied to brewing.

Today, New Beer’s Eve is celebrated in a much lighter spirit, often with tastings, brewery tours and gatherings with friends. DaysOfTheYear.com suggests hosting beer tastings, trying local brews or visiting a nearby brewery as popular ways to mark the occasion.

Across the country, breweries and beer brands often join in the celebration. National brands like Anheuser-Busch, which famously delivered beer to the White House in 1933 using its iconic Clydesdales, continue to lean into the holiday through promotions tied to National Beer Day.

Closer to home, Mississippi’s growing craft beer scene offers its own way to celebrate. Breweries such as Lazy Magnolia Brewing Company in Kiln and Southern Prohibition Brewing in Hattiesburg have helped fuel the state’s craft beer boom, reflecting a national shift toward more diverse and locally brewed options. NationalToday.com notes craft beer has surged in popularity in recent decades as drinkers seek new flavors and styles.

Beer itself has a long and global history, dating back thousands of years. NationalToday.com says evidence of early barley beer dates to around 3400 B.C., and ancient civilizations such as the Babylonians and Egyptians even incorporated beer into daily life and labor systems.

Despite its ancient roots, modern beer culture continues to evolve. From light lagers to bold craft brews, the variety available today would have been unimaginable during Prohibition.

Health experts still emphasize moderation. NationalToday.com defines moderate drinking as up to one drink per day for women and up to two for men.

For many, though, New Beer’s Eve is less about quantity and more about appreciating history, community and a cold drink shared among friends.

After all, as Roosevelt reportedly remarked when beer made its return in 1933, it was simply “a good time for a beer.”

Prohibition, which lasted from 1920 to 1933, outlawed the production and sale of alcohol nationwide. Britannica.com notes the ban created widespread demand for faster policy change as the nation faced economic hardship during the Great Depression and sought new sources of jobs and tax revenue.

When restrictions were lifted, even partially at first with low-alcohol beer, it jumpstarted breweries and related industries. Historical accounts cited by DaysOfTheYear.com indicate the return of beer helped revive manufacturing, agriculture and transportation sectors tied to brewing.

Today, New Beer’s Eve is celebrated in a much lighter spirit, often with tastings, brewery tours and gatherings with friends. DaysOfTheYear.com suggests hosting beer tastings, trying local brews or visiting a nearby brewery as popular ways to mark the occasion.

Across the country, breweries and beer brands often join in the celebration. National brands like Anheuser-Busch, which famously delivered beer to the White House in 1933 using its iconic Clydesdales, continue to lean into the holiday through promotions tied to National Beer Day.

Closer to home, Mississippi’s growing craft beer scene offers its own way to celebrate. Breweries such as Lazy Magnolia Brewing Company in Kiln and Southern Prohibition Brewing in Hattiesburg have helped fuel the state’s craft beer boom, reflecting a national shift toward more diverse and locally brewed options. NationalToday.com notes craft beer has surged in popularity in recent decades as drinkers seek new flavors and styles.

Beer itself has a long and global history, dating back thousands of years. NationalToday.com says evidence of early barley beer dates to around 3400 B.C., and ancient civilizations such as the Babylonians and Egyptians even incorporated beer into daily life and labor systems.

Despite its ancient roots, modern beer culture continues to evolve. From light lagers to bold craft brews, the variety available today would have been unimaginable during Prohibition.

Health experts still emphasize moderation. NationalToday.com defines moderate drinking as up to one drink per day for women and up to two for men.

For many, though, New Beer’s Eve is less about quantity and more about appreciating history, community and a cold drink shared among friends.

After all, as Roosevelt reportedly remarked when beer made its return in 1933, it was simply “a good time for a beer.”

item.title: MSDH Recognizes National Public Health Week Across Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
The Mississippi State Department of Health is joining agencies and organizations across the country in recognizing National Public Health Week from April 6-12.

Those include perinatal and infant services, child and adolescent services, adult health, vital records and statistics, regulatory services, WIC, communicable disease prevention, county health departments, rural health and physician workforce programs, EMS and acute care systems, the opioid and substance use program, epidemiology and the Mississippi Medical Cannabis Program.

MSDH is encouraging the public to follow along through the MSDH Healthy Mobile App and on its website for updates during the week.

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: Emmanuel Williams, Choctaw County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
CHOCTAW COUNTY — A year and a few months after he was last heard from, very little is known about what happened to Emmanuel Williams, and those who love him are still searching for answers.

Williams, 38, has been missing since December 2024, according to information from Missingsippi.org, a nonprofit that tracks missing persons cases across the state. He was last in contact with family members in Ackerman around that time and has not been heard from since.

Described as a Black male with black hair and brown eyes, Williams is about 5 feet 8 inches tall and weighs approximately 140 pounds. His sudden disappearance and lack of communication understandably raised concerns among loved ones.

According to Missingsippi.org, Williams has ties to the Little Rock, Arkansas, area and could possibly be there. However, no confirmed sightings or updates about his whereabouts have been publicly reported.

With very few details available online or in a search of Newspapers.com, his case highlights the uncertainty many families face when a loved one goes missing. There is no publicly released information that can be easily found about the circumstances surrounding his disappearance.

Williams’ family remains concerned for his safety and is hoping someone may have seen him or has information that could help bring him home.

Anyone with information about Emmanuel Williams is encouraged to contact [email protected] .

As time passes, advocates say sharing the little-known cases like Williams’ is critical to keeping attention on missing persons across Mississippi and helping bring them home.

item.title: Lowndes County man sentenced to more than 13 years for meth trafficking - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
COLUMBUS — A Lowndes County man has been sentenced to more than 13 years in federal prison for trafficking methamphetamine, authorities announced.

Calvin Baskin, 55, of Columbus, was sentenced to 157 months in prison after previously pleading guilty in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi. The charge stems from his arrest on Aug. 8, 2024, according to court documents.

In addition to the prison term, Baskin was ordered to serve five years of supervised release following his incarceration.

U.S. Attorney Scott F. Leary said the case reflects ongoing efforts by law enforcement to combat drug-related crime in Mississippi communities.

“Some communities here face daily violence driven by the illegal drug trade,” Leary said. “This investigation and prosecution reflect the daily vigilance exhibited by state and federal law enforcement.”

Officials said Baskin was convicted of trafficking more than 50 grams of methamphetamine.

Drug Enforcement Administration Assistant Special Agent in Charge Anessa Daniels-McCaw said the sentence underscores the seriousness of drug trafficking offenses.

“Methamphetamine trafficking brings nothing but misery and crime to our doorsteps,” Daniels-McCaw said. “This sentence reflects the gravity of the threat posed by illegal drugs and the power of interagency cooperation.”

Lowndes County Sheriff Eddie Hawkins also praised the collaboration among agencies involved in the case.

“This sentencing sends a clear message that those who traffic illegal drugs and endanger our communities will be held accountable,” Hawkins said.

The case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Lowndes County Sheriff’s Department, the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics and the U.S. Marshals Service. Assistant U.S. Attorney Clyde McGee prosecuted the case.

Officials said the case is part of broader federal initiatives, including the Homeland Security Task Force and Project Safe Neighborhoods, which focus on reducing violent crime and dismantling drug trafficking organizations.

item.title: Laurel man arrested in connection with Howard Industries arson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Cash Matlock
item.description:
LAUREL — A Laurel man wanted in connection with a vehicle fire at an industrial site has been arrested, authorities said.

The Jones County Sheriff’s Department initially sought Rashad Lawrence, 30, on a charge of arson following a March 31, 2026, incident at Howard Industries in the Pendorff community.

Deputies and the Laurel Fire Department responded to reports of a vehicle fire at the facility, where investigators later determined that three passenger vehicles in the parking lot had been damaged. Authorities identified Lawrence as the suspect.

The sheriff’s department had asked the public for help locating Lawrence and said a financial reward could be available through Jones County Crime Stoppers for information leading to his arrest.

In an update, officials said Lawrence has since been taken into custody. According to the sheriff’s department, he peacefully surrendered to Deputy Jarone Walker at a residence in the Currie community.

The arrest stems from the ongoing investigation into the March 31 vehicle fire at Howard Industries.

No additional details about charges or court proceedings were immediately released.

item.title: Jackson to receive $26.5M in state projects for roads, parks, arts and infrastructure - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — More than $26 million in state-funded projects are headed to Jackson, targeting roads, parks, infrastructure and cultural institutions across the capital city and Hinds County.

City officials announced the funding, included in Senate Bill 2189, the 2026 legislative projects bill, will bring approximately $26.52 million in total appropriations within Jackson city limits.

Of that, about $5.67 million will go directly to City of Jackson projects, including road paving, park improvements and neighborhood infrastructure work. The largest portion, $19 million, will support local nonprofit organizations focused on recreation, education and the arts.

Hinds County is also set to receive more than $7.2 million in additional funding, with about $1.85 million of that benefiting projects within Jackson.

Mayor John Horhn praised the collaboration between city leaders, lawmakers and state officials.

“Jackson is moving forward because so many people rolled up their sleeves and went to work for our city,” Horhn said. “When we stay at the table and keep advocating for Jackson, we can deliver results for our residents.”

Among the city-funded projects, $4 million is designated as matching funds for federal highway and road improvements along key corridors including Woodrow Wilson Avenue, Medgar Evers Boulevard and McDowell Road. Other allocations include $750,000 for infrastructure improvements in northwest Jackson, $400,000 for Westside community projects and $200,000 to pave a portion of Hanging Moss Road.

Parks and recreation projects will also see investment, including $250,000 for upgrades to the Pete Brown Golf Facility and $70,000 for tree removal at Leavell Woods and Sykes Park.

A significant portion of the funding will support nonprofit partners. LeFleur’s Bluff Conservancy is set to receive $13 million for improvements at LeFleur’s Bluff State Park, while Mississippi Children’s Museum will receive $5 million to expand exhibits and programming. Additional funding includes $650,000 for the Mississippi Museum of Art and $350,000 for the Mississippi Symphony Orchestra to support music programs.

Regional projects funded through Hinds County include $500,000 for sewer and drainage improvements in the Presidential Hills neighborhood, $100,000 for neighborhood security cameras in several Jackson communities and $750,000 for repairs at Parham Bridges Park.

The Jackson Municipal Airport Authority will also receive $500,000 in matching funds for infrastructure upgrades.

Horhn also credited local partners, including the Jackson City Council, Hinds County Board of Supervisors and community organizations, for helping secure the funding.

While noting ongoing challenges such as long-term infrastructure needs, Horhn said the investment signals continued progress for the city.

item.title: Jackson State launches Industry Access Series with Lionsgate executive - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Jackson State University will launch a new speaker series Tuesday aimed at connecting students with industry leaders, beginning with a conversation featuring a top Hollywood marketing executive.

The inaugural session of “THEE Industry Access Series: From JXN to the Industry” will feature Briana McElroy, executive vice president and head of worldwide digital marketing at Lionsgate. The event is scheduled for 11 a.m. to noon in the Dollye M.E. Robinson Liberal Arts Building on campus.

University officials said the series is designed to give students and the Jackson community direct access to professionals across a range of fields, offering mentorship, career insight and networking opportunities that connect classroom learning to real-world experience.

Tuesday’s discussion will highlight McElroy’s career path from Jackson to a senior leadership role in the film industry, as well as her work on major movie marketing campaigns. Organizers said the conversation will also explore the impact of historically Black colleges and universities and community ties on career development.

The session will be moderated by Callie Callicut, a Jackson State senior majoring in journalism and media studies and a member of the university’s women’s track and field team.

Jackson State is hosting the event as part of its Research Engagement Week. Officials said students attending will gain insight into how large-scale film campaigns are developed and what it takes to break into the entertainment industry.

McElroy currently leads digital marketing strategy for major film releases, including projects that have incorporated HBCU culture, such as marching band performances.

The event is open to students, faculty and the community, and light refreshments will be provided, according to the university.

item.title: Former Southeast Greene Water Authority Manager Arrested on Embezzlement Charge - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
SOUTHEAST GREENE – A former office manager for the Southeast Greene Water Authority has been arrested on allegations that she embezzled money from the water authority for personal use, according to the Mississippi Office of the State Auditor.

State Auditor Shad White announced that special agents with his office arrested Deborah Harper, the former office manager, in connection with the case.

According to the auditor’s office, Harper allegedly took cash payments made through new customer water agreement forms and converted the money for her own personal use. Investigators also allege that she used payments made by other water customers to cover water bills for herself and her daughter.

“The dedicated team at the State Auditor’s Office will continue to work closely with prosecutors to get record results, one case at a time,” White said in a statement.

If convicted, Harper could face up to $25,000 in fines and up to 10 years in prison.

The auditor’s office noted that all persons arrested by the Mississippi Office of the State Auditor are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

The office also encouraged the public to report suspected fraud through the auditor’s website or by calling 1-800-321-1275 during normal business hours.

item.title: DARKHORSE DOGS: The sweetest, calm Baby Hippo needs a forever home - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
Corinth – Corinth-Alcorn Animal Shelter is hoping to find a forever home for Baby Hippo, an 8-year-old dog described as a gentle and affectionate companion.

Despite her name, shelter staff say the 60.6-pound dog is “100% baby” and has a soft, loving personality.

Baby Hippo came to the shelter after she was picked up as a stray. Officials said no owner ever came forward to claim her.

Shelter staff say she is fully vaccinated and heartworm positive, but her treatment will be covered. They said she would do best in a home without cats.

According to the shelter, Baby Hippo is a calm dog who enjoys staying close to her person and would thrive in a home with a steady routine, a soft bed and plenty of love.

Those interested in adopting Baby Hippo can learn more through the Corinth-Alcorn Animal Shelter adoption page.
